subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & $/1M tokens target
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@hyperlytics.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Demo — next steps and rough pricing targets

Thanks again for the time today, Sarah — quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can size a dedicated pool and surface cost scenarios.

Key inputs from the call (please correct anything I mis-captured):
- Workload: customer-facing assistant + nightly batch re-ranker for search
- Expected steady-state: ~120M tokens / month (spikes up to ~200M in seasonality)
- Avg tokens per request: ~150
- Target latency SLO: 200–400ms (p50/p95) for the assistant path
- Peak concurrent requests estimate: ~10–18 RPS sustained, short bursts to ~60 RPS
- Budget range discussed: $6k–$12k / month for inference (top-level)
- Desired unit economics: target <$75 per 1M tokens (you said $60–$75 was ideal)

As next steps we promised:
1) Quick capacity sketch (GPU type options + lanes) for the above profile
2) Price scenarios (reserved 1/3/6/12-months, pilot PO) and an effective $/1M tokens estimate
3) A short pilot plan (duration, acceptance criteria, rollback) if you want to validate throughput and latency

I've attached the deck we demo'd and a first-pass pricing workbook; Ben/Marcus and I will pull an initial sizing and two price bands (A100 preference, and H100 option). Can you confirm the steady-state 120M/month and the budget band above? Also, is a 3-month pilot acceptable before a quarter-commit reserved contract?

Attachment: demo-deck.pdf

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Re: Intro / Demo — next steps and rough pricing targets

Thanks, Ben — that's accurate and well captured. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirm steady-state: yes, plan for ~120M tokens / month out of the gate. We do expect a campaign-driven spike to ~200M for a 2–3 week window, but that's not sustained.
- Avg tokens/request: 150 is right for assistant payloads; re-ranker runs are heavier but batched overnight.
- Budget: we currently have a procurement headroom of $6k–$12k/mo for inference; with the right unit economics we can stretch to $15k/mo but would need SLAs and predictable billing cadence.
- Pilot: 6-week pilot is preferred (we want traffic-shaping + production monitoring in that window)

Two asks for your sizing: can you show both (A) an A100-based reserved lane and (B) an H100-based lane, with the expected effective $/1M tokens for each under a 3-month vs 12-month reserve? Also, we care about node counts for handling bursts to 60 RPS without latency degradation.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Product, HyperLytics
sarah@hyperlytics.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@hyperlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & $/1M tokens target

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clarity. We're preparing two clean scenarios and a recommended pilot configuration. High-level notes on what we'll include in the pricing sheet so you can compare apples-to-apples:

What we'll model in the workbook:
- GPU family options: A100-80GB and H100-class (we'll include H100 price/throughput delta)
- Reserved lanes (1, 2, 4 GPU lanes) with burst capacity options and autoscale policy notes
- Conversion of throughput to token consumption and effective $/1M tokens under each commitment term (3m / 12m)
- Est. on-call/enterprise SLA uplift and any enterprise add-on fees (audit logs, private VPC)

Preliminary thumb-rules (for planning, rough numbers):
- For your profile (~120M/mo, peaks to 200M): a 2-GPU reserved pool (A100-80GB) often covers steady-state with short bursts if we enable burst lanes (extra GPU) and smart routing; H100 lanes can reduce required GPUs for the same SLOs, which improves effective $/1M but has different reserved pricing.
- Effective $/1M tokens: preliminary range we'll show: A100 reserved band ~ $70–$95 per 1M tokens; H100 reserved band ~ $50–$75 per 1M tokens. These are illustrative — final numbers depend on model, quantization (Q4_0 vs Q8), and whether you choose prefix caching for the assistant path.

Pilot suggestion:
- 6-week pilot (you prefer 6 weeks — we can do that). Recommended pilot configuration: 2x A100-80GB reserved lanes for baseline, plus 1 burst H100 node for high-concurrency windows to prove scaling and fallbacks. Acceptance: <400ms p95 for assistant path during business hours across 2 weeks of live traffic; verify token consumption metrics and billing reconciliation.

I'll attach a capacity projection CSV and a pricing scenarios workbook in the next email. If that plan looks good, Ben and I will draft a pilot statement of work and a sample PO.

Thanks,
Irene

If helpful, Marcus can run a quick bench on our staging weights (same model family) once we align on the model/quantization choices. Marcus — can you take the bench and put numbers into the pricing workbook this afternoon?
